messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] 02:34 UTC - KV cache eviction spike detected in us-west-2. Affected models: llama-2-mqa-7b, mistral-7b-v1.85. Symptoms: p99 token latency >250ms, elevated error rates.

alex: grabbing dashboards now. p99 token latency jumped from ~80ms to ~320ms on multiple runtime shards. KV miss rate up to 27% on shard s-11, eviction_rate trending upwards.

marta: metrics snapshot: eviction_rate: 42k/s, kv_hits: 73%, avg_batch_size: 24 -> dropped to 4. Looks like prefix churn feeding continuous-batching -> lots of unique KV keys.

sam (oncall): paging runtime + routing. @kevin can you check routing? hypothesis: MQA traffic being pinned to small KV pools.

kevin: checking routing logs. There's a surge of long-context requests (200-400 tokens) to llama-2-mqa-7b. Continuous batching aggregated them poorly; many unique prefixes are inserted into small pools with short TTLs -> eviction thrash.

natalie: customer impact: support tickets up (12 in last 10m). Two paid customers have SLO breaches. Notifying CS and preparing comms.

marta: quick mitigations I propose: 1) disable continuous_batching for the affected MQA/GQA models in us-west-2; 2) increase max_entries for impacted KV pools (s-11/s-12); 3) deploy ingress-level prefix dedupe; 4) temporarily prefer larger pools for GQA routing.

sam (oncall): executing step 1. Pushing runtime config patch to turn off continuous batching for llama-2-mqa-7b and mistral-7b-v1.85 in us-west-2.

sam (oncall): command used:
```
POST /admin/models/llama-2-mqa-7b/config/_patch
{ "continuous_batching": false }
```

deploy-bot: runtime-config-hotfix (PR #4227) started rolling to us-west-2: canary 5% -> 25% -> 100%.

alex: canary nodes show p99 down to ~180ms. That's promising.

kevin: applying KV pool sizing tweak to shard group s-11/s-12:
```
kv_pools:
  - name: mqa-hotfix-pool
    max_entries: 200000
    eviction_policy: lru
```
Applying now.

marta: note: mistral-7b-v1.85 is on the GQA routing codepath. GQA combined with continuous_batching and long prefixes produced many low-reuse entries. Will add fallback to route GQA traffic to higher-capacity pools.

sam (oncall): live checklist update:
- disable continuous batching for MQA/GQA models (done)
- increase kv pool sizes (in progress)
- temporary routing to larger pools for GQA (in progress)
- deploy ingress prefix dedupe (planned)
- monitor customer impacts and error budgets

kevin: opened PR #4231 to add prefix dedupe (bloom filter) at ingress and bump TTLs for large-prefix entries. Initial canary shows dedupe dropping ~18% of duplicate long-prefix inserts.

kevin: canary deploy for #4231 in progress. Early metrics: insertion rate down, eviction_rate falling.

natalie: CS update sent: "We observed a KV cache eviction storm affecting inference latency for specific models in us-west-2. Mitigations are being rolled: disabling aggressive batching and increasing cache pools. Estimated recovery 30-45 minutes." :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: runtime-config-hotfix PR #4227 fully rolled to us-west-2 (commit 9f3b2c4). No rollback.

alex: post-rollout stats: p50 ~60ms, p95 ~140ms, p99 ~130-160ms depending on model. Major improvement vs 320ms.

kevin: still seeing a small class of scripted clients hammering with repeated long prefixes that yield near-zero reuse. Suggest adding a prefix dedupe cap and a max-prefix-length guard in ingress for MQA models.

marta: implemented TTL bump for large-prefix entries and the ingress dedupe in PR #4231: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/4231. Also updated pool templates for persistence.

sam (oncall): action items assigned:
- @kevin: finish canary and promote PR #4231 (ETA 20m)
- @marta: persist kv pool sizing in config for us-west-2 (ETA 10m)
- @alex: incident writeup + customer-impact summary (ETA 30m)

kevin: canary shows ingress bloom filter preventing ~18% of redundant inserts and reduces unique key churn. Latency stabilizing further on canary nodes.

natalie: CS follow-up: two customers that saw timeouts had requests retried by clients; no persisted inference data lost. We'll schedule account-specific RCA calls.

alex: drafting incident summary for postmortem. Highlights:
- root cause hypothesis: interaction between continuous_batching and KV cache TTLs under long-prefix MQA/GQA workloads causing eviction storms.
- contributing factors: routing of high-volume long-prefix traffic to small pools; lack of ingress dedupe for scripted clients; TTL and pool sizing not tuned for long-prefix patterns.
- mitigations applied: disabled continuous_batching, increased pool sizes, deployed prefix dedupe, temporary routing to larger pools.
- customer impact: elevated p99 and transient timeouts for a small cohort; no data loss.
- followups: add per-model defaults for continuous_batching thresholds, per-model pool-sizing heuristics, load tests for long-prefix churn, add alert: kv_eviction_rate > 10k/s per pool.

marta: adding followups: add max-prefix-length guard in request router, and evaluate adaptive TTLs for large prefixes.

sam (oncall): metrics stable for ~40 minutes. Downgrading incident severity P2 -> P3. Continuing to monitor for 2 hours, then hand to postmortem owners.

incident-bot: [RESOLVE] 03:41 UTC - Incident P2 -> P3. Resolution posted to #incidents-log.

natalie: coordinating customer followups and scheduling RCA calls with affected accounts.

alex: thanks all for rapid triage. I'll finish the postmortem with runtime + routing + product.

kevin: added short-run synthetic test to staging for long-prefix churn: https://internal.redwood/tests/long-prefix-churn/. Please run before next rollout.

marta: tagging postmortem owners: @alex (lead), @marta (runtime), @kevin (routing), @natalie (customer-impact).

sam (oncall): handing off to daytime oncall. Ping me if it recurs, otherwise closing pager. :white_check_mark:
